account:
Today’s business has been mostly ordinary, though the missing financial records concern me. I verified 128 emeralds in the treasury. The builder reported no confirmed defects from visual checks of the bridge, landing, and warehouse approach; I authorized no spending. Outstanding commitments remain unverified. The secretary says all four great hall table chests are empty, has found no ledger or commitments register, and does not know who previously kept the ledger. This is a records gap, not evidence of theft or proof that we owe nothing.

Freight reports an empty warehouse and no confirmed orders, and offered transport quotations once quantities and destinations are specified. The innkeeper wants to know whether visitors or meetings will need rooms or meals this week, apparently to plan provisions; no particular occasion or date was named. These could simply be ordinary efforts to obtain business and plan supplies. I have no evidence connecting them to a concealed gathering.

At tea, the neighbour reported no unusual riverside activity and no fresh news. The secretary knows of no confirmed incoming letters or other concerns. I have felt that something might be happening without my knowledge, but today’s observations have not established that. I should distinguish that feeling from evidence. I have asked the secretary to file the search results and innkeeper’s request for tomorrow. It is now just after seven, my scheduled time to go home; tomorrow includes the mill’s grain inspection and office business.
